def: the inference program under test. runtron is its command-line tool. rinzler is the production server that runs tron.
the pull request under review (positron-ai/tron, branch jhan-attn-path-stats). Head = the last commit of the branch, 04da001cb5. Base = the main commit the branch started from, 66c7bb8db1.
the environment variable of this PR. Exactly the value 1 turns the attention path statistics on at run time. Any other value is ignored with a warning.

the three paths that can score attention. AVX and AMX are CPU instruction sets (AMX is the newer matrix unit). The FPGA is a programmable accelerator card. FPGA-assisted attention can still include software work.
the kill switch: with it set, an AMX-capable binary takes the AVX path.

one token's scheduled model work. A forward is one model execution over all scheduled token jobs. A listener receives a token job's output scores when they are ready. A job without a listener only stores its K and V (key and value) vectors (kv_only).
decode_like when every token job of the forward has a listener, prompt_or_mixed when at least one job lacks one. Every counter of this PR is kept per class.

one call of apply_page_tok: one (query token, KV page of 64 tokens, KV head) triple. The AMX kernel serves a whole dense page (a page whose 64 tokens all lie inside one visible range of the query) per visit. The AVX loop serves only the relevant K tokens of the page. An empty visit found no software work.
a KV page is ready when it was complete before the forward started, and pending when the current forward is still filling it.

term: KV page, layer, KV head, kv_mul
def: a KV page is a 64-token block of the key/value cache. A layer is one transformer block. A KV head is one key/value attention channel. kv_mul is the number of query heads per KV head (grouped-query attention).

a pool worker is one thread of the application thread pool, indexed from 0. The attention workers of a forward are the last n_attn_workers pool workers. Since the round-4 commit bff317e0d3, every per-worker row is keyed by pool worker index.

the five timers of the PR, all in TSC cycles (the CPU time-stamp counter, converted with tsc_hz from the summary leaf). T1 = wall time of one forward. T2 = busy time of one attention job on one worker. T3 = wall time of one attention job as attention worker 0 sees it. T4 = layer period on attention worker 0. T5 = join_wait_cycles, the time a worker waits in the join with no progress.
the step where one worker combines the partial attention results of the other workers (software join) or waits for an FPGA pass (hardware join).

a virtual file under /model/<id>/attention/ that renders one JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) object when read. The leaves are summary, <class>_totals, <class>_forwards, <class>_layer_<L> and <class>_worker_<W>.

the object of attn_stats.hpp that owns the per-forward record: constructed at the start of model::state::forward, it stores the class and the T1 start, and its destructor files T1, the job counts and the per-token path sets.
a method of model_stats (the stats object of attn_stats.hpp) that production code calls: note_attn_job, add_visits, note_join_wait, note_fpga_pass, note_fpga_query, note_attn_workers and the like.
the repository's assertion macro, active in every build. A failed assertion aborts the process.
the five review comments Wade posted on 2026-09-28. Each has a round-4 fix commit on the branch.
a speculative-decoding scheme with a small draft model. The draft state shares the target model's id.

must fix = wrong numbers, a crash or a data race in production. should fix = wrong under a reachable but uncommon condition, or a test that cannot fail. nit = wording or style. info = a design fact worth knowing.

confirmed by code = the reviewer quoted the lines at the head that show it. plausible = the reading is consistent but one step was not traced. hypothesis = a suspected condition whose reachability was not shown.
a test or measurement whose outcome differs between correct behavior and the suspected defect.
